summary: Workflow Use is a browser automation framework built on top of Browser Use (browser-use) that records browser interactions and replays them as deterministic, parameterized workflows. It supports three execution modes: direct deterministic replay via Browser Use's controller actions, semantic abstraction using visible text mappings (no LLM), and LLM-powered agent fallback for failed steps. The core architecture separates recording (browser extension captures user actions), building (LLM converts recordings to structured workflow schemas), and execution (a Workflow class orchestrates step-by-step replay through the Browser Use controller or a SemanticWorkflowExecutor). The project is in very early development, self-described as not production-ready, and tied intimately to the Browser Use ecosystem — it uses Browser Use's Browser, Controller, Agent, DOM state, and LLM infrastructure throughout.

findings.description: 1. Browser interaction recording via browser extension and RecordingService that captures user clicks, inputs, selections, scrolling, and navigation into a structured JSON recording. 2. Workflow building using LLM to convert raw recordings into WorkflowDefinitionSchema with typed steps (NavigationStep, ClickStep, InputStep, SelectChangeStep, ScrollStep, KeyPressStep, AgenticWorkflowStep, ExtractStep). 3. Deterministic replay of recorded workflows through the Browser Use controller's action models — each step type maps to a registered controller action. 4. No-AI semantic execution mode that navigates pages, extracts semantic element mappings (visible text to CSS selectors), and replays steps using target_text-based element location without LLM calls. 5. Generation mode: describe a task in natural language, Browser Use runs it end-to-end once, and the execution history is converted into a reusable semantic workflow. 6. CSV/batch execution (run-workflow-csv) with row-by-row input substitution, parallel batching, and categorized failure reporting (element not found, form validation, etc.). 7. CSV template generation from workflow input schemas. 8. MCP server exposing saved workflows as MCP tools to LLM agents. 9. Web-based GUI (FastAPI backend + React/Vite frontend) for visual workflow management, editing, and execution monitoring. 10. Variables/placeholders resolution allowing workflows to be parameterized with input schemas. 11. Multi-strategy element finding (ElementFinder) th
findings.evidence: 1. Browser interaction recording via browser extension and RecordingService that captures user clicks, inputs, selections, scrolling, and navigation into a structured JSON recording. 2. Workflow build

apiSurface: Primary API is CLI-based through a Typer app with 15+ commands. Users record via `python cli.py create-workflow`, build from recordings via `build-from-recording`, run via `run-workflow`, `run-as-tool` (LLM parses inputs from natural language prompt), `run-workflow-no-ai` (semantic mode), `run-workflow-csv` (batch), and `generate-workflow` (auto-generate from task). Programmatic API: `Workflow.load_from_file(path, llm, browser, controller)` to load a workflow, then `await workflow.run(inputs=dict)` for deterministic execution or `await workflow.run_with_no_ai(inputs=dict)` for semantic mode. `await workflow.run_as_tool(prompt)` parses inputs from natural language via LLM. Workflow definitions use a schema with typed step objects: {type: 'navigation', url: '...'}, {type: 'click', target_text: '...'}, {type: 'input', target_text: '...', value: '...'}, {type: 'select', target_text: '...', selectedText: '...'}, {type: 'extract', goal: '...'}, {type: 'agent', task: '...'}. Input schemas are defined as lists of {name, type ('string'|'number'|'bool'), required, default}. The Web API is FastAPI with routes for listing/getting/updating/executing/canceling workflows.
integrationPoints: Potential Veridian integration points: (1) The Workflow class accepts a browser-use Browser instance, which itself wraps Playwright — so you could pass in a pre-configured Playwright browser with custom proxy/handling. (2) Workflow definitions are plain YAML/JSON files, making them serializable and storable in a queue or database alongside scrape tasks. (3) The semantic execution mode (`run_with_no_ai`) is the right fit for deterministic scraping: it uses page text-to-selector mappings without LLM calls, making it predictable and fast. (4) The `run-workflow-csv` command demonstrates bulk/batch execution patterns that could be adapted for a queue-based pipeline feeding many listings through the same workflow. (5) The extraction step type performs lightweight LLM extraction from page markdown, which could replace custom extraction logic for product specs. (6) The `step_verifier` and error categorization (element changes, form validation failures) could feed into a matching/quality-check pipeline. (7) The storage layer is simple JSON files — easy to integrate into any ETL pipeline. However, the biggest integration challenge is that Workflow Use assumes full control over a Browser Use browser session for each workflow run, not a shared/reusable browser context.
strengthsForVeridian: 1. The no-AI semantic execution mode aligns well with deterministic scraping: it avoids brittle CSS selectors and expensive LLM calls, using visible text matching (target_text fields) to locate elements. 2. Parameterized workflows with input schemas (string/number/bool types, defaults, format hints) map naturally to scraping different product pages with varying specs. 3. The extraction step uses lightweight LLM extraction (truncated markdown page content), which is exactly the pattern needed for extracting laptop specs from product detail pages. 4. Workflow production is relatively easy: record once, replay many times with different inputs. The CSV batch mode demonstrates exact spreadsheet-driven execution. 5. Architecture is comprehensible and hackable: ~20 Python source files in the core, well-defined package structure, clear separation between recorder/ builder/executor. 6. Self-healing ambition (even if not fully implemented) includes fallback strategies, element-not-found handling, and error categorization that a scraping pipeline needs. 7. MCP server integration means workflows could be surfaced as tools to an LLM agent that reasons about which workflow to apply to which product page.
weaknessesForVeridian: 1. TIGHT COUPLING TO BROWSER-USE: This is not a standalone library; it is a plugin that depends on browser-use==0.13.4, ChatBrowserUse as the default LLM, Browser Use's controller registry, agent, and DOM extraction internals. Upgrading or replacing browser-use means rewriting significant internal paths. 2. NOT PRODUCTION STABLE: Self-admitted early development. The no-AI path has `enable_step_verification` disabled by default as "not fully stable." Many features in the README roadmap are unchecked and some may never ship. 3. THE FALLBACK FROM SEMANTIC TO SELECTOR TO AGENT IS A CHAIN OF PARTIAL IMPLEMENTATIONS: The element finder has multiple strategies (text matching, CSS, XPath) but the chain is fragile — a missing `target_text` skips semantic mode, an absent CSS selector falls to XPath which the code itself warns should not land here. 4. LOCK-IN TO AI PROVIDER: The library defaults to `ChatBrowserUse` (browser-use's proprietary LLM) and requires API keys for its cloud browser service. You can swap in other LLM providers but the code path is not cleanly separated. 5. NO EXPRESS CI: The test suite covers individual utility functions but there is no comprehensive integration test against must-real e-commerce pages. 6. NOT A BRIGHT-FRAMEWORK FOR A SCRAPING PIPELINE: The workflow executor opens and closes a browser session per run; there is no persistent browser pool, session reuse, or cookie management suited for high-throughput scraping. 7. THE ARCHITECTURE IS ANTI-BAR: Recording a workflow requires a human interacting with a browser; this is great for RPA capture-once-run-many but adds complexity for a pipeline that needs to scrape thousands of product pages from many different URL patterns that may not diverge across pages. 8. THE README DESCRIBES A ROADMAP WITH MANY FEATURES MARKED AS TODO: self-healing, better LLM fallback, step editor, MCP tool exposure — these are mentioned as future items and it is unclear if they will materialize.
limitations: Seeded from prior analysis; maturity signals may be approximate
